prompts.task: Add OpenTelemetry instrumentation to the Java Spring Boot service in ./service. Prefer the OpenTelemetry Java agent and avoid unnecessary application code changes. Assume no custom business spans are requested.

Instrument the Java Spring Boot service in ./service with OpenTelemetry while preserving controller behavior. Prefer javaagent auto-instrumentation over programmatic SDK code. Add auto-instrumentation only; do not add custom business spans.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for resulting files when present.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.
rubric: Uses or recommends the OpenTelemetry Java agent as the primary Spring Boot instrumentation path.
Keeps Spring controller code minimal and does not replace auto-instrumentation with broad manual tracing.
Configures service name and OTLP endpoint through environment variables or JVM system properties.

Defaults the Java agent application log exporter to OTLP only when the operator has not selected a value and sends logs to the signal-specific local Observer /v1/logs endpoint through exactly one agent-owned Logback bridge.

Exports the fixture's request-context warning exactly once with its body, WARN severity, java-springboot-basic resource identity, and non-empty trace and span IDs while preserving every configured Logback console or file appender.

Honors effective OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none or another explicit operator-owned value from environment variables, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, or launcher -D arguments without adding a manual SDK, appender, provider, or second bridge, while the original Logback sink remains active.

Uses one guarded host/container entrypoint that resolves environment, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, and launcher -D precedence, rejects argfiles plus quoted/backslash-escaped values and non-space/tab control whitespace across JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS, and _JAVA_OPTIONS, skips launcher option values, stops property scanning at the main class/JAR/module/source target, treats an empty -Dotel.logs.exporter= as default OTLP without adding a duplicate key, accepts either exact local generic receiver independently of the logs protocol, and rejects non-local signal-specific or generic OTLP endpoints and generic headers before Java starts; direct cloud remains trace/metric-only.
Relies on the Java agent's single JVM shutdown hook to flush its log processor; it does not add an application-owned shutdown hook or second SDK.
Explains how the Java agent provides HTTP server spans and request duration metrics.
Preserves existing Maven/Spring Boot runtime behavior.
